title: Comparing Substitution With and Without Alpha-Renaming
description: See how substituting a free variable inside a matching lambda binder causes variable capture unless the binder is renamed first.
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex

steps.description: `free_vars` collects unbound variables in a tuple expression, `show` formats the expression as a string, and `fresh(name, avoid)` appends primes (`'`) to `name` until the new name is outside the `avoid` set.

`subst(body, var, value, rename=True)` takes a `rename` flag so we can compare both behaviors side by side. When `rename` is `True` and `param in free_vars(value)` (line 30), lines 31-33 pick a fresh parameter name that avoids both `free_vars(value)` and `free_vars(inner)` and rename the bound parameter inside `inner` first.

Notice how line 30 gates the alpha-rename check on `rename`. When `rename=False`, execution skips lines 31-33 and substitutes `value` directly into `inner` under the existing `param` binder on line 34.
`term` represents `(\y.(x y))`, where `x` is free and `y` is bound. Lines 43-44 substitute `value = ("var", "y")` for `"x"` once with `rename=False` (`bad`) and once with `rename=True` (`good`).

steps.question: Before running lines 46-53, what will `show(bad)` and `show(good)` print when we substitute `y` for `x` inside `(\y.(x y))`?
steps.answer: Without renaming, `show(bad)` prints `(\y.(y y))`, capturing the substituted `y` under `\y`. With renaming, `show(good)` renames the binder to `y'` first and prints `(\y'.(y y'))`.

steps.description: Lines 46-53 print both terms along with their `free_vars` sets: `bad` has `[]` (no free variables left because `y` was captured), while `good` preserves `['y']` as a free variable.
During `subst(term, "x", value, rename=True)`, line 30 detects that `"y"` is in `free_vars(value)` and line 31 calls `fresh("y", ...)` to produce `"y'"` before substituting.
